blocks.text: Computer networks are classified based on size and coverage area. Different types of networks are used for different purposes. Each type connects devices in a specific way. The most common types are LAN, WAN, and the Internet (Public WAN). These networks help in communication and data sharing. Understanding network types helps in proper network selection.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: Computer networks are classified based on distance and coverage area.

A Local Area Network connects devices within a small area (as shown in Figure 1.3). This area can be a home, school, or office. LAN provides high data transfer speed. It is usually owned and managed by a single organization. Ethernet and Wi-Fi are commonly used in LANs. LAN is cost-effective and easy to maintain.

blocks.alt: A house cut open with a LAN badge: a router with three antennas high on the wall is cabled to a desktop and a laptop on a table, to a tablet on the wall and to a second router on the floor; the floor router is cabled to a printer and reaches the tablet by Wi-Fi. A TV stands on a dresser.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.3: Local Area Network (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.3).

blocks.text: A Wide Area Network covers a large geographic area (as shown in Figure 1.4). It connects networks in different cities or countries. WAN uses leased lines, satellites, or the Internet. Data transfer speed is slower than LAN. WAN is expensive to install and manage. The Internet is the largest example of a WAN.

blocks.alt: A WAN badge; three clouds labelled Internet are joined by dashed links, and each cloud is linked to a site with a Wi-Fi router: two homes with computers and a phone, and an office building with a desktop computer.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.4: Wide Area Network (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.4).

blocks.text: The Internet is a global network connecting millions of devices. It allows sharing of information worldwide. Services like email, websites and cloud storage use the Internet (as shown in Figure 1.5). It uses standard protocols for communication. The Internet supports education, business, and entertainment. It plays an important role in daily life.

blocks.alt: A globe in the centre, joined by lines to devices all around it: two desktop computers, a laptop, a router, a printer, a server and several clouds with Wi-Fi signs; some devices are also linked to each other.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.5: Internet (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.5).

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Students list services that use the Internet. Discuss its importance.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text:
• DSL(Digital Subscriber Line) : Internet through telephone lines; allows calling and browsing at the same time.
• ISP (Internet Service Provider): Company that provides Internet access to users.
